claims: reducing $3 a fortnight per $1,000 above that
whys: The figure is correct, but it is typed into the text instead of read from PENSION_ASSETS_TEST.taperPerThousand.single, which the assets-test FAQ on line 34 uses. If the constant changes, this answer will drift.

claims: Deeming applies ... or if it belongs to your partner and they are 60 or older.
whys: This partner condition does not match the usual CSHC grandfathering rule. That rule turns on whether the stream and the card have both been held since before 1 January 2015. Please check it against the DSS Social Security Guide for CSHC deeming of account-based income streams.

claims: You can change the percentage online twice a financial year.
whys: As far as I know, Services Australia lets families change their CCS withholding percentage at any time in their online account, with no twice-a-year limit. Needs checking against the Services Australia CCS withholding page.

claims: a single homeowner with {formatAUD(433_000)} of assessable assets is {formatAUD(100_000)} over the limit, so the pension drops by {formatAUD(300)}
whys: The example's excess ($100,000) and reduction ($300) are typed literals, not calculated from PENSION_ASSETS_TEST.fullPensionLimit.single.homeowner (333,000) and taperPerThousand.single. They match today. When the limit is indexed on 1 July, the text will drift while assetsTestRate() in the same sentence updates, so the example will contradict itself.

claims: Work Bonus: the first $300 of employment income each fortnight ... the 100-hour work rule.
Work Bonus: first $300 of employment income each fortnight; 100-hour work rule.
whys: $300 and 100 hours are typed literals, while the next answers use CP.workHoursLimit. If the Work Bonus amount or the hours limit changes, this answer will drift from the constant.
These are literals, while line 36 uses CP.workHoursLimit. They can drift from the constants.
constants: CARER_PAYMENT.workHoursLimit plus a Work Bonus constant in lib/constants/centrelink-income-test.ts

claims: Resolution Scheme tiers: under $200 full debt; $200 to $1,999 gets $200; $2,000 to $4,999 gets $400; $5,000+ gets $600.
whys: The tier amounts are typed literals, while the max payment comes from RESOLUTION_SCHEME.maxPayment. If the constant changes, the two could drift apart.

claims: SG on commission applies 'up to the quarterly maximum contribution base'.
whys: Payday Super starts on 1 July 2026. My understanding is that it turns the maximum contribution base into an annual amount, so 'quarterly' may be out of date for the 2026-27 page. The FAQ answer at commission-tax-faqs.ts line 54 only says 'maximum contribution base', so the two places do not match.
constants: SUPER_GUARANTEE (lib/constants): add a maximum contribution base period/value

claims: Commission can lift a HECS-HELP repayment 'into a higher band' (same wording in commission-tax-faqs.ts line 66: 'higher repayment band').
whys: From 2025-26, compulsory HELP repayments use a marginal system on income above the threshold, not the old percentage bands. 'Band' may describe the pre-2025 system.
